dedupe_keys.name: ilee quakecore shake table test of a 2 storey low damage concrete wall building

description: ILEE-QuakeCoRE Shake table test of a 2-storey low-damage concrete wall building is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "experimental", published or maintained by Rick Henry, University of Auckland (aucklanduni.ac.nz). To provide essential evidence to support the development of low-damage (or resilient) concrete structures, a system level shake-table test of a 2-storey low-damage concrete wall building was conducted on the multi-functional shake-table array at Tongji University. The test building used post-tensioned (PT) precast concrete walls and precast concrete frames with slotted beam connections. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "experimental" project. Keywords: shake table test; reinforced concrete; low-damage; seismic resilient design; post-tensioned wall; slotted beam; wall-to-floor connection; energy dissipating devices;. Published 2021-06-10. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
